newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil imports may be computerized from next month.
newsitem.headline: Brazil imports may be computerized from next month.

text.p: The Brazilian government may start publishing as soon as February trade balances within a few days of the end of each month, said Mauricio Cortes, secretary of foreign trade at the Ministry of Industry and Commerce.
Cortes told reporters a new computer system registering imports had been suffering some teething problems, but would certainly be up and running in the first quarter of 1997.
To date, exports have been registered in a computer system while imports were collated by hand, resulting in monthly trade balances only being available towards the middle of the following month.
"From February, you won't have this situation of exports being revealed first and the trade balance in the middle of the next month," Cortes said.
He later added, under heavy questioning about claims the computer system was not working, that all problems would be solved in the first quarter of this year.

Describing the computer system as "perhaps the most advanced of its kind in the world", Cortes said the introduction of automized documentation was a sign of Brazil's willingness to make its trade situation as transparent as possible.
